payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
node.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order. Interpret their reported findings, not merely execution statuses. Complete requires established edited paper-and-cup identity, positive cup-entry evidence, and established completed stuffing from s2. Partial requires positively established requested entry or intermediate stuffing into a cup together with affirmative incompleteness from s2. Absent requires affirmative exclusion of requested progress: established wholly external placement, established rim-only placement without stuffing action, or adequately visible absence of a required object, corroborated or explicitly reconciled by s2. Unresolved candidate identity does not defeat absent if grounded spatial evidence independently excludes entry into any receiver, but identity uncertainty and missing positive cues cannot supply that exclusion. Unknown applies whenever a fact necessary for the applicable conclusion remains unresolved or conflicting observations lack grounded reconciliation. A pass on s1 or the nested boundary-mapping check supplies assessed evidence only; neither earns requested progress or completion credit. A mapping pass with unresolved entry must remain unresolved unless s2 independently supplies the missing grounded finding. Failure of completion alone never establishes absent. Dependent agreement is not independent confirmation. Infer no new visual facts.

Direct comparison does not establish that the edited reddish object corresponds to the source cup. The images allow a grounded inventory, but edited cup identity and source-to-edit correspondence remain unresolved.

The paper’s right edge and lower portion lie in front of the reddish rounded object, whose visible contour and dark curved line do not establish a cup opening or enclosing cup walls. No paper segment is visibly disappearing behind a receiver boundary; the hand obscures only the paper’s upper-left region, not a demonstrated contact with the reddish object. No alternative receiver is established. Receiver identity: unresolved. Geometry: established wholly external placement—the visible paper is in front of the object, and its visible outline does not enter it. Requested progress: excluded. Completion: excluded.
